newsitem.title: USA: PaineWebber answers SEC probe of yield burning.
newsitem.headline: PaineWebber answers SEC probe of yield burning.

text.p: PaineWebber Group Inc. said Tuesday the Securities and Exchange Commission has asked it for information about a Dade County, Fla., debt refunding as part of the SEC's broad probe of excessive markups of Treasury securities sold to municipalities.

The company is among 16 that make up Dade County's bond underwriting pool. The county asked all 16 to describe any investigations or litigation undertaken by federal or state authorities in connection with their public finance activities since the pool was formed in 1995.

PaineWebber said in its response that it, "along with many firms," had responded to SEC subpoenas and requests for information about municipal advanced refunding escrow transactions of at least $100 million over a four-year period.

"Among the transactions falling into that category is the escrow provided in connection with the Dade County Health Facilities Authority Hospital Revenue Revenue Refunding Bonds. Series 1993A (Baptist Hospital of Miami Project)," PaineWebber wrote in its reponse to the county.
The markups, known as yield burning, give the appearance of complying with federal tax restrictions on investment earnings but provide a windfall to the bond-market middleman.

PaineWebber said it had not been charged with any violation and had not received notification known as an SEC Wells notice, which indicates a more advanced probe into the matter. The company was senior manager for the $115 million advanced refunding issue.
It was unclear whether the SEC had specific concerns about that issue, or whether it sought the information merely because the issue exceeded the $100 million benchmark.
SEC investigators in Miami declined to comment.
A PaineWebber spokesman in New York said its policy prohibited comment because the investigation is continuing.

Another investment member, Prudential Securities Inc., told the county that the SEC had asked it for documents as part of the yield burning probe. The SEC's interest in that issue, a 1993 issue by the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, has already been reported. No charges have been filed.
